newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil called $1.00 to $1.50 up, Brent firmer.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil called $1.00 to $1.50 up, Brent firmer.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures were called to open $1.00 to $1.50 a tonne higher on Monday while Brent was expected to open near the $19.00 mark having traded at that level on SIMEX.

May gas oil, which expires at 1100 GMT on Monday, closed $1.75 a tonne higher on Friday at $170.75 a tonne. Open interest as of Friday was 13,976 lots, and traders were expecting a delivery of up to 500,000 tonnes.
June Brent closed 25 cents firmer at $18.94 a barrel on Friday and on SIMEX on Monday the front-month contract reached $19.00 a barrel for the first time in nearly six weeks.
"Nineteen dollars is the key issue today, but I'm pretty confident we'll break through it," a broker said.
Higher resistance was pegged at $19.27 a barrel.
Traders said that short-covering on the NYMEX crude contract on ACCESS out-of-hours trading had taken the June contract above $20.50 a barrel and was supportive for Brent.

The launch of new wargames by Iran in the Gulf on Sunday was also supportive, brokers said, with a top U.S. military commander pledging to defend the strategic Strait of Hormuz against any Iranian threat.
